The sample's own slope looks the same in the field, so subtract the slope from QCAL-sampletilt. Sensor tilt shows only /M on the object side (1° at the sensor ≈ 0.1° at 10x), so a gradient is almost always objective or sample tilt. Needs ~1 µm Z steps at 20x (depth of field ~3 µm). The Z-sweep half of MTG-13; MTG-13 keeps distortion. Done when two runs agree within 0.05° and a deliberately tilted objective is reported with the right sign

title: Sample-holder tilt from the stage: autofocus at the via-grid corners and far points, plane in µm/mm
note: the via grid spans 6 mm; plate and holder corners give the long baseline. FR4 warps up to 0.75 % (~1 mm over 127 mm), so the PCB is a tilt reference over a few mm only: measure the warp of a few Rev E plates first and use glass (QCAL-glass) for the whole holder. Testable on the virtual microscope with set_focus_surface(tilt_x, tilt_y). Done when the holder tilt is reported with its screw turns (QCAL-screws)

title: Kinematic screw geometry of holder, objective and objective mount: positions, thread pitch, turn direction
note: from the CAD: each screw's position in camera x/y and its pitch, so a tilt turns into 'screw B, quarter turn clockwise'. Stored per stand in the setup JSON. Decide together with MTG-16 (turning one mount)

title: Alignment guide with signed screw turns from the calibration, re-measured until within tolerance
note: extends the landed MTG-14 guide (unsigned sharpness map) with the measured sign and amount. Done when a misaligned FRAME is brought within tolerance in at most two rounds

title: Illumination axis from the focus sweep: lateral walk of the via per µm Z and the flat-field centroid
note: oblique light shifts a feature sideways when defocused: tan(angle) = dx/dz of the via image during the focus sweep the calibration already runs, so this costs no extra motion. The flat-field centroid against the sensor centre gives the lateral offset of the light. Done when an LED moved off axis is reported in mm and degrees; on LED-matrix rigs the centre pixel can then be picked in software

title: Flat field per objective and light source, taken through the open round cutout, used in live view and stitching
note: dark frame from the read-noise wizard, bright frame defocused through the ⌀6 mm open hole (larger than the field at 4x and up). Optional correction in the live view, the stitcher and the writers. Done when the seams of a stitched well are gone (edge-to-centre ratio within 2 %)

title: Axial and lateral colour per objective: focus offset and image shift per LED colour or fluorescence channel
note: focus and via position at R/G/B of the LED matrix (and each filter set); stored as a Z offset per channel and applied on channel switch. Done when switching channels needs no refocus

title: Z backlash: focus approached from above and below at the via; autofocus always approaches from one side
note: the XY backlash step exists; Z has none. Pairs with MTG-18 (true Z step). Done when autofocus repeatability is within a quarter of the depth of field

title: Autofocus defaults per objective from the measured focus curve (width, step, range)
note: the calibration already records a focus curve per objective; store its width in the objective slot and derive autofocus step and range from it. Done when autofocus needs no hand-tuned parameters after a calibration run

title: Glass targets in the plate: chrome cross grating and a sub-resolution pinhole array, Rev F pockets
note: decide between dedicated pockets in a Rev F plate and filling the existing round/rect cutouts. The cutouts are landmarks today (the axes step tracks the round hole as a dark blob, the placement check uses the rect edges), so filling them means re-testing those steps. One target with MTG-15 (grid in the correction target), not two

title: Resolution map across the field: slanted-edge MTF at nine field points per objective
note: ISO 12233 on chrome edges of the cross grating; the routed PCB edges are too rough. A lopsided MTF50 map flags tilt or decentring independently of QCAL-tilt. Done when MTF50 per field point is stored and shown per objective

title: 3D PSF per objective from sub-resolution pinholes or beads: NA check, spherical aberration, coma direction
note: needs ≤0.5 µm pinholes (chrome on glass, a mirror with apertures in reflection) or 100-200 nm beads; the 0.3 mm vias are far larger than the PSF

title: One-minute image-quality check: focus width, tilt sign, flat-field ratio, MTF50 against the stored calibration
note: runs at the via; warns when a value drifts past tolerance and keeps a history (calibration age for NSW-HEALTH). Done when a loosened objective is flagged by the check before the next scan
